questions.question:
Direction: Study the data carefully and answer the following question.

Two series (I) and (II) are given below, with wrong term P is series (I) and wrong term Q in series (II).

(I): 6, 20, 47, 83, 132, 196

(II): 11, 15, 20, 31, 45, 67

Find that P is what percent of Q?
questions.explanation:
Logic in series (I):

6 + \(4^{2}\) = 22(20)

22 + \(5^{2}\) = 47

47 + \(6^{2}\) = 83

83 + \(7^{2}\) = 132

132 + \(8^{2}\) = 196

So, wrong term in the series = P = 20

Logic in series (II):

11 + 2 × 2 = 15

15 + 3 × 2 = 21(20)

21 + 5 × 2 = 31

31 + 7 × 2 = 45

45 + 11 × 2 = 67

So, wrong term in the series = Q = 20

Required percentage = \(\frac{20}{20}\  \times \ 100\) = 100%

questions.question:
Direction: Study the data carefully and answer the following question.

A series is given with one wrong term in it.

25, 35, 20, 40, 15, 55

If a new series is formed, whose 1st term is the wrong term of the given series and follows the same pattern as in the given series, then find that the 5th term of the new series will be equal to the which term of the given series?
questions.explanation:
Logic in the given series:

25 + 10 = 35

35 - 15 = 20

20 + 20 = 40

40 - 25 = 15

15 + 30 = 45(55)

So, the wrong term in the given series = 55

Now,

1st term of the new series = 55

2nd term of the new series = 55 + 10 = 65

3rd term of the new series = 65 - 15 = 50

4th term of the new series = 50 + 20 = 70

5th term of the new series = 70 - 25 = 45

So, the 5th term of the new series will be equal to the 6th term of the given series, which will come in place of the wrong term.
